title: Choose the visual world
question: Safer hand: three familiar directions from Rafiqi's own world, plus the category standard. Pick one, or re-roll.

options.label: Conversation Thread
options.lineage: the chat thread and shared location pin everyone uses to arrange a meeting
options.thesis: Rafiqi told as the conversation that sets up a meeting: request, accepted, location, I have arrived.
options.viewport: Headline on one side; on the other a short example thread: your request, the volunteer accepting, a location card with the pin, and the yellow 'volunteer arrived' pill.
options.risk: Chat bubbles are familiar to the point of cliché; the thread must be labelled as an example and stay readable to screen readers.

options.label: Appointment Slip
options.lineage: the booking slip and queue ticket from hospital and ministry visits
options.thesis: Every request is a slip with a number, a date, a time and a place, and the page is built from them.
options.viewport: A large request slip (#481, date, start and end time, meeting point) beside the headline, its torn stub holding the download buttons.
options.risk: Can feel like an events-ticketing site if the slip turns decorative instead of carrying the real request details.

options.label: Metro Map
options.thesis: Your route and the volunteer's are two lines that meet at an interchange station.
options.viewport: Two coloured lines cross the hero and meet at an interchange marked with the pin; the steps below are stations along the line.
options.risk: Closest to the current route motif, and transit diagrams are a common how-it-works trope.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean mobile-app landing page at the craft level of Be My Eyes, Careem and Sehhaty.
materials: real app screens in device frames
canonCard.viewport: Headline with the real app screens, a short benefit row, the steps, and a download band.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every app page by design; the craft has to carry it.
